newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Second Australian suicide using euthanasia law. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Second Australian suicide using euthanasia law. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: A second person has killed herself under a euthanasia law in the Australian outback region of the Northern Territory, an association promoting voluntary euthanasia rights said on Monday.

Dr Robert Marr of the Coalition for Voluntary Euthaniasia said Mrs Janet Mills died last Thursday after she administered a lethal dose of drugs to herself, assisted by euthanasia campaigner Dr Philip Nitschke.

"On Thursday morning, January 2, Janet Mills became the second person to use the NT (Northern Territory) Rights of the Terminally Ill Act," the coalition said in a statement released on its "Deliverance" Internet site.
Cancer patient Bob Dent, 66, was the first person to take his own life under the regional law, which took effect in July 1996 and has been opposed by politicians in the national parliament.
Mills, 52, had a rare form of skin cancer called mycosis fungoides which caused her skin to disintegrate.
She had appealed to the medical community before Christmas for a specialist to give her the approval she needed to go ahead with the procedure.
Mills killed herself using a a computer-driven device to self-administer a lethal dose of drugs, the coalition said.
The world's first euthanasia law came into effect in July last year in the lightly-populated outback region of the Northern Territory.
Dent became the first person to use the law the following September.
Mills said in a letter written the day before her death and also released on the Internet that she had no hesitation in asking for euthanasia.
"I believe that euthanasia is the greatest thing for people who are sick with no chance of getting better," she said.
"It's a wonderful idea and it stops people from suffering when they don't need to."

In December the Australian parliament's lower house, the House of Representatives, voted to overturn the voluntary euthanasia law. The anti-euthanasia bill will go before the upper house Senate this year (corrects from next year) for final approval.
